title: Quasi-finiteness at a prime is zero fibre dimension at that point
statement: Let $\varphi:R\to T$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings of finite type [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. Let $\mathfrak q\subset T$ be prime and $\mathfrak p=\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$. Put $F=T\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, where $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is the residue field [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Let $\overline{\mathfrak q}\in\operatorname{Spec}F$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] be the unique prime contracting to $\mathfrak q$ [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-ring-primes-bijection]. Then $\varphi$ is quasi-finite at $\mathfrak q$ [def-weil-pbc-ring-map-quasi-finite-at-prime] if and only if $\dim_{\overline{\mathfrak q}}\operatorname{Spec}F=0$, where dimension at a point is the minimum of the Krull dimensions of its open neighbourhoods [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point].

source.place: Tag 0397, label lemma-locally-quasi-finite-rel-dimension-0, applied to Spec T -> Spec R; the second proof identifies isolated points with points of dimension zero in the locally Noetherian fibre.

proof.text: Put p = q.comap(algebraMap R T), F = p.Fiber T and let x be the canonical fibre prime. Mathlib Algebra.FiniteType.baseChange makes F finite type over p.ResidueField. Algebra.FiniteType.isNoetherianRing and PrimeSpectrum.instNoetherianSpace make Spec F Noetherian. Every subspace is Noetherian, and prime spectra and their subspaces are T0.

Unfold quasi-finiteness to openness of {x}. An open singleton has discrete subspace topology and dimension at most zero. For any open neighbourhood U of x, the closure of x in U is an irreducible closed subset, so dim U is nonnegative. The infimum of neighbourhood dimensions is at most the dimension of the singleton and at least zero, hence equals zero.

If the local dimension is zero, it is less than one. Apply iInf_lt_iff twice to obtain an open U containing x with dim U < 1. Dimensions take values in WithBot ENat, so dim U <= 0. Apply the existing topological theorem lem-sc-zero-dim-noetherian-closed-finite with ambient U and closed subset univ. It gives finiteness of U and closedness of all its singleton subsets. Thus U is finite and T1, hence discrete.

The singleton of x in U is open by discreteness. The subtype inclusion of the open U in Spec F is an open map, and its image is {x}. Thus {x} is open in Spec F, precisely the definition of quasi-finiteness at q.
